title: Veil and Crown
premise: Jonah Thornbury has spent her life as a royal food-taster in the Veiled Valley, the one place in the old kingdom of Cael where magic cannot follow — and the only reason she, born with the gift, has survived it. When the new crown declares a hunt for all gifted citizens and her immunity to poison marks her as one of them, Jonah flees into a country that officially no longer exists, guided by rumors of a door that leads beyond magic's reach. Hunted by the crown's inquisitor and shadowed by the last dragon, whose dying fire is the only key that can open that door, Jonah must decide whether survival means escape or sacrifice. In the end she chooses neither: she spends the dragon's final flame not on the door but on burning the crown's registry of the gifted, then returns to the valley — alive, unmarked, and carrying an inheritance of silence instead of power.
about_author: Edmund Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the legal fictions by which vanished countries are declared to still exist. He writes fantasy about people trapped inside other people's paperwork.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She tastes the king's breakfast, detects bitter almond in the honeyed pears, and saves a steward's life while concealing why she noticed. Establishes her double life: immune by gift, safe only because the valley suppresses magic. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into fear when the steward asks how she knew.

chapters.title: One Dish at a Time
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, flashback-woven. How she was apprenticed at nine, dosed deliberately to build tolerance, and taught never to ask questions. Her mother's parting words — 'the valley forgets you if you let it' — haunt her. Emotional beat: tenderness for her dead mentor, grief she's never named.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Criers announce the Gift Registry Act: all gifted persons must present themselves or be hunted. The valley's protection is now a cage — registration would mean leaving it. Emotional beat: dread arriving like weather; the whole market square goes silent together.

chapters.title: What the Valley Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She maps the valley's boundary stones with old Wenna, a hedge-healer, learning the veil's mechanics and its one flaw: it protects only those inside. Emotional beat: the strange comfort of a border that loves you conditionally.

chapters.title: The Steward's Debt
chapters.summary: Steward Aldric's POV. Saved by Jonah once, he now must report suspected gifted staff under the Act. His chapter dramatizes institutional corruption: he burns his own doubts along with evidence. Emotional beat: self-loathing disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Knock at the Kitchen Door
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. An inquisitor's clerk arrives to interview kitchen staff. Jonah lies fluently, but the clerk notices her untouched wine glass. Emotional beat: terror performed as boredom.

chapters.title: Wenna's Warning
chapters.summary: Wenna's POV. She recognizes what Jonah is — her own sister was taken in the last purge — and urges flight before the net closes. Gives her a token: a cold iron key with no lock. Emotional beat: inherited fear passed hand to hand like an heirloom.

chapters.title: Flight Across the Stones
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She slips past the boundary at dawn; sensation floods back — color too bright, her gift waking like a limb gone numb. Behind her, the valley closes. Emotional beat: vertigo and exhilaration braided together.

chapters.title: A Country That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Outside the valley she finds Cael proper: roads signed for towns struck from maps, waymarkers in a dead royal line's heraldry. She learns the kingdom was 'dissolved' after the Dragon War, yet its laws persist. Emotional beat: uncanny homesickness for a place she's never been.

chapters.title: The Hunt Begins
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serane Voss's POV. Introduced as brilliant, sincere, genuinely believing the gifted are a plague risk. She takes over the valley file and finds Jonah's name flagged. Emotional beat: righteous certainty — the reader should almost agree with her.

chapters.title: The Guttering Light
chapters.summary: Dragon POV (first of few). The last dragon, Ember-that-Remains, dying in the Ashreach mountains, feels Jonah's gift ignite across the distance like a struck bell. Dragons can smell the door-seal. Emotional beat: ancient loneliness.

chapters.title: Roadside Kindness
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A smuggler caravan takes her in; the matriarch, Odile, charges nothing but loyalty. First warmth since flight. Emotional beat: cautious trust, the luxury of being fed by someone else's hands.

chapters.title: Registry of Names
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She interrogates valley records, finds Wenna's testimony, and pieces together the iron key's significance: keys were cut during the Dragon War for those meant to survive. Emotional beat: the hunter falling in love with the puzzle.

chapters.title: The Burned Village of Harrowmere
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She passes through a town purged the month before — ash, chalk marks, a child's shoe. Understands what capture means. Emotional beat: horror that hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: Odile's Price
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The caravan is stopped at a checkpoint; Odile sells information about a 'kitchen girl' to buy passage — but gives Voss the wrong direction. Moral compromise rendered intimately. Emotional beat: guilt worn like a coat she refuses to take off.

chapters.title: The Door in the Mountain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Following war-era survey fragments, she reaches a sealed gate in the Ashreach foothills — the door out of dissolved Cael. It rejects her key: the lock wants fire, not iron. Emotional beat: hope arriving and immediately demanding more than she has.

chapters.title: Ember-that-Remains
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She climbs toward the dragon's caldera, half-hoping for death, and instead meets something that speaks in embers and remembers her grandmother's name. Emotional beat: awe dissolving fear into kinship.

chapters.title: Bargain of Ash
chapters.summary: Dragon POV. Ember offers his last flame to open the door — but flame spent is life spent, and he asks what Jonah will carry forward if he dies for her. No answer yet. Emotional beat: gravity of a gift not yet accepted.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Ascendant
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Promoted after a successful purge, she begins keeping her own private registry — names she quietly omits. Power's first small corruption shown from inside. Emotional beat: ambition tasting like medicine.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Voss's riders corner her at a river ford. She escapes only by using her gift openly for the first time — tasting the water's poison trail to find safe crossing — confirming everything. Emotional beat: survival costing her invisibility.

chapters.title: What Survives Us
chapters.summary: Wenna's POV, interlude. Wenna is arrested in the valley and refuses to give up Jonah, reciting instead the names of every gifted person she's buried. Emotional beat: defiance as inheritance; the theme of legacy made explicit.

chapters.title: The Interrogation of Wenna Thornbury
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss interviews Wenna and is shaken by her composure; for the first time she files a report containing a lie of omission. Emotional beat: a crack in certainty, hairline but real.

chapters.title: Refuge Among Ruins
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Wounded, she shelters in a dissolved monastery whose monks kept the old kingdom's archives — including the door's true history: it was built to let the guilty flee, and it has never once opened. Emotional beat: despair metabolized into stubbornness.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Confession
chapters.summary: Brother Cassian's POV. The last monk admits the order helped build the registry centuries ago; every purge descends from their careful lists. He begs Jonah to destroy what they made. Emotional beat: shame seeking absolution through action.

chapters.title: Two Keys
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Comparing Wenna's iron key with archive drawings, she realizes the key isn't for the door — it's for the registry vault beneath the capital, where every gifted name ever recorded is kept. Emotional beat: revelation reframing her whole journey.

chapters.title: Downriver to the Capital
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She joins a grain barge crew, working kitchens again, tasting her way unnoticed through checkpoints. Skills honed in captivity become tools of freedom. Emotional beat: competence as quiet joy.

chapters.title: The Crown's Kitchen
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Using forged papers, she takes a taster's post in the royal palace itself — directly above the vault. Full-circle irony: the job that endangered her becomes her cover. Emotional beat: nerve-shredding calm.

chapters.title: Serane's Doubt
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Tasked to vet palace staff, she interviews the new taster and cannot shake familiarity. She checks the valley file against her memory and finds the discrepancy she herself created weeks ago. Emotional beat: the hunter hunting herself.

chapters.title: Night of Long Knives' Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. On the eve of the Great Purge ceremony, the palace prepares to burn the registry publicly as theater while adding thousands of new names. Jonah watches the scaffolds rise. Emotional beat: dread at scale; individual stakes swallowed by machinery.

chapters.title: The Vault Below
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She descends through service tunnels with Cassian's maps and opens the registry vault — shelves of ledgers, centuries of names, hers among them, her mother's above it. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Fire Needs a Keeper
chapters.summary: Dragon POV. Ember, near death, flies toward the capital unbidden — dragons keep their bargains. He lands in the ceremonial square as the Purge begins, causing chaos. Emotional beat: sacrificial grandeur, terrifying and beautiful.

chapters.title: The Purge Interrupted
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Amid panic, Jonah reaches the vault entrance where Voss confronts her — key in hand, both women recognizing each other fully at last. Emotional beat: two survivors of different machines facing off.

chapters.title: Inquisitor and Thief
chapters.summary: Alternating Jonah/Voss POV. Their confrontation becomes an argument about survival: Voss argues order requires lists; Jonah argues lists are how the dead are made. Voss hesitates — and her hesitation costs her standing as guards close in. Emotional beat: persuasion as combat.

chapters.title: The Last Flame
chapters.summary: Climax. Ember offers his final fire to Jonah at the vault mouth. She could open the door and flee forever. Instead she turns the flame on the registry itself. Ledgers burn; Ember gutters out mid-roar; Voss, given the choice, steps aside. Emotional beat: sacrifice transmuted into inheritance — she inherits not power but responsibility.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The burning registry scatters names as embers; across the city, the marked feel their papers die. The Purge collapses without its lists. Jonah carries Ember's last scale out of the smoke. Emotional beat: exhausted, hollow triumph.

chapters.title: What Voss Did Next
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She falsifies the official account — blaming a vault accident — erasing Jonah and herself from the story. Corruption turned to mercy; the same tool, reversed. Emotional beat: redemption that refuses to call itself that.

chapters.title: The Door Unopened
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She returns to the mountain gate one last time. Without dragon-fire it stays shut, and she finds she no longer wants it open. Some doors are answers to questions you stop asking. Emotional beat: peace with an unlived life.

chapters.title: Homecoming
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. She crosses back into the Veiled Valley, gift going quiet, and buries Ember's scale beside her mother's grave. Wenna's name is added to the stone. Emotional beat: mourning folded into belonging.

chapters.title: The New Taster
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, years later. She trains an orphan girl with a suspiciously accurate tongue, teaching her everything — including when to lie, when to run, and which names to remember. Emotional beat: inheritance completed; the cycle gentled but not broken.

chapters.title: Veil and Crown
chapters.summary: Final chapter, omniscient coda. The valley keeps its secret; the crown keeps its fiction; somewhere a door waits under ash. Jonah, old now, tastes the morning air and smiles at nothing. Emotional beat: quiet permanence — survival as a thing handed down, not held.
